newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's office was discussing with the police about setting up a demonstration area outside his office.

-- MING PAO -- A report by China's Senior Procuratorate to the National People's Congress on Tuesday will stress hostile forces inside and outside China are trying to "westernise" and "split" China, which was a threat to stability.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen will deliver a report on the work of the Preparatory Committee to the National People's Congress, in which he will describe the situation of Hong Kong as encouraging and stress that the provisional legislature has its legal basis.
-- The commander of the People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison said that the army will raise the Chinese national flag in Hong Kong on July 1.
-- APPLE DAILY -- A survey showed that Hong Kong people discriminated against mainland immigrants, believing that mainland immigrants were ignorant, dirty and rude.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Bank of East Asia was positively developing businesses in the Asia-Pacific and planning to acquire financial organisations in the region.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen will underline the power of the Preparatory Committee to set up the provisonal legislature in an attempt to check challenges to the legality of the controversial body.

-- China Poly Group, the investment arm of the People's Liberation Army, is expected to approve an injection of assets into its HongKong-listed vehicle, Continental Mariner Investment, by the end of the month.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Frontier legislator Emily Lau called on democrats to boycott Hong Kong's first elections under mainland rule if the voting system was changed to favour pro-China candidates.
